newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Life says to sell auto, fire cover to firms.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Life says to sell auto, fire cover to firms.

text.p: Nippon Life Insurance Co said on Thursday that it would start selling auto and fire insurance to corporations capitalised at more than 100 million yen when its non-life insurance subsidiary starts business from October.

"We don't have any voluntarily agreement to restrict sales of those products," said a Nippon Life spokesman. "It is the sales strategy (of the subsidiary) and we don't plan to restrict such sales at all."
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun newspaper said on Thursday that Japan's life insurers have until now followed a self-imposed policy preventing non-life arms selling such cover to corporate customers.
Spokesmen at major life insurers, however, declined to comment on the Nihon Keizai report.

"It is up to management policy," said a Dai-ichi Mutual Life Insurance Co spokesman, adding that there are Finance Ministry guidelines under which life insurers must consider measures if needed in order not to jeopardise existing non-life insurers.

Analysts said that non-life insurance companies have been worried that life insurers, who have large stock portfolios, would likely benefit from selling auto and fire insurance products to companies through subsidiaries.
In Japan an amendment to a law on the insurance market took effect in April, allowing insurers to conduct both life and non-life insurance business through subsidiaries.
In August, 11 Japanese non-life insurance firms and six life insurance companies set up subsidiaries to enter each other's business from October.

Some industry sources said, however, insurers are gradually easing into the deregulated market to avoid any radical change in the business environment. "We want to ensure job security in the industry, and don't want to implement any radical change," a source said.
